title: Surface weak ferromagnetism
abstract: This paper proposes a model of a Néel-ordered antiferromagnet exhibiting a weak ferromagnetic moment restricted to the crystal surface, generated by spin-orbit coupling induced by broken surface symmetries. Depending on crystal termination, the surface magnetic moment can align with identical or opposing signs on the top and bottom surfaces, resulting in a zero Faraday effect paired with a finite Kerr effect upon reflection for the latter configuration.
summary: This theoretical work proposes a mechanism where weak ferromagnetism appears at the surface of an antiferromagnet due to broken crystal symmetries interacting with spin-orbit coupling. By analyzing symmetry constraints on the electronic Hamiltonian, the authors show that while the bulk magnetic moment cancels out, the surfaces retain a net magnetization, leading to distinct magneto-optical signatures.
main_problem: The paper models the emergence of weak ferromagnetism at the surface of an otherwise Néel-ordered antiferromagnet.
main_result: Surface symmetry breaking, induced by spin-orbit coupling, stabilizes a net magnetic moment solely at the boundaries, leading to unique magneto-optical responses like a finite Kerr effect with zero Faraday effect for certain terminations.
method: The analysis uses tight-binding models and detailed symmetry group theory (time-reversal, mirror reflection) applied to the fermionic Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is an antiferromagnet modeled by two stacked layers (A and B) with N\'eel order. The physics is governed by a Hamiltonian incorporating spin-orbit coupling ($\lambda$) terms arising from broken surface symmetries.
key_observables:
Surface weak ferromagnetism ($	ext{M}_z 
eq 0$), Faraday effect, Kerr effect, Berry curvature ($\Omega_{\pm}^{xy;k}$), and Dzyaloshinskii invariants.
important_parameters: Spin-orbit coupling strength ($\lambda$), interlayer interactions (antiferromagnetic/ferromagnetic), and the specific crystal termination geometry.
main_assumptions: The bulk cancellation of spin-orbit coupling is attributed to field compensation between top and bottom layers, while surface effects break this symmetry.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the two-layer unit cell, the necessary symmetry operations (e.g., breaking $xy$ plane mirror reflection), and the resulting structure of the Rashba-type spin-orbit coupling terms ($	ext{d}_1, 	ext{d}_2, 	ext{d}_3$).
paper_structure: The paper develops the model by first defining the Hamiltonian for the stacked layers, then using symmetry analysis to show why bulk magnetization cancels out, and finally demonstrating how surface termination breaks these symmetries to induce a net surface magnetic moment.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the detailed use of symmetry invariants (like Dzyaloshinskii's) and band structure calculations involving spin-orbit coupling is highly relevant for understanding topological properties in quantum materials that might interface with AMO systems.
